rules.statement: Keep presentational UI components stateless and prop-driven: they must not read from the Redux store, call RTK Query hooks or perform side effects, and may hold local state only when it is intrinsic to the control.
rules.why: Stateless presentational components render in Storybook and under React Testing Library without a store; putting state in them breaks that isolation and is a review failure.
rules.check: Look for useSelector/useDispatch, RTK Query hooks, fetch calls or effects with side effects inside shared design-system or presentational components rather than in a screen-level container.

rules.statement: Put state and side effects in container components at the top of each screen, which wire Redux and RTK Query and pass data down to presentational components as props.
rules.why: Keeping state wiring in one place keeps the layers clean so each can be tested on its own.
rules.check: Look for store wiring spread across deeply nested components, or screens with no container that still manage server state below the top level.

rules.statement: Move non-trivial logic such as validation, transforms, PKCE, discovery parsing and boundary rules out of React components into UI-free service or helper modules that have their own unit tests.
rules.why: Logic kept in components cannot be unit-tested directly and breaks the stateless/stateful/service layering.
rules.check: Look for validation, parsing, crypto or transformation logic written inline in .tsx components, or new helper logic added with no direct unit tests.

rules.statement: Use RTK Query endpoints for server state, with tag-based cache invalidation, and write hand-rolled thunks or ad-hoc fetch calls only when there is a clear exception.
rules.why: RTK Query gives one consistent model for server and client state, with cache tags and devtools.
rules.check: Look for new createAsyncThunk, raw fetch or axios calls that load or change server data and that could have been an RTK Query endpoint.

rules.statement: Do not bake environment or tier configuration (API base URLs, issuer, auth endpoints, feature flags) into the frontend bundle at build time; load it at runtime from the serving host's discovery or bootstrap document before the app renders.
rules.why: A bundle is built once and must run unchanged in sandbox, test and production, and build-time config invites mismatches between config and bundle.
rules.check: Look for import.meta.env / process.env tier values, hardcoded API or issuer URLs, or per-environment build modes used to pick endpoints.

rules.statement: Import shared frontend workspace packages only through their public entry point (the package name), never through deep or relative paths into another package's source.
rules.why: Clean package boundaries let the packages be pulled out into another repository by moving folders, without rewriting source.
rules.check: Look for imports like '../../packages/x/src/...' or '@scope/pkg/src/internal' that cross a workspace package boundary.

rules.statement: Take colors, typography and other brand values from the centralized theme provider tokens instead of hardcoding them in components.
rules.why: Theme tokens sit behind a provider so per-tenant branding can be injected later without changing components.
rules.check: Look for hardcoded color hex values, font families or spacing literals in components where a theme token should be used.

rules.statement: Give each shared presentational component a Storybook story.
rules.why: Storybook is how components are checked in isolation, and it depends on them being stateless.
rules.check: Look for new or changed shared presentational components that have no matching *.stories.tsx file.

rules.statement: Make the issuer in a frontend bootstrap or discovery document default to the serving tenant's configured issuer, never one taken from the request origin or Host header.
rules.why: Deriving the issuer from the request would let the caller control an authority value that must belong to the tenant.
rules.check: Look for bootstrap or discovery endpoints that build the issuer from HttpRequest.Host, Scheme or Origin instead of the tenant's issuer.
